vocabulary.example: I go to work by bus.
She rides a bicycle to school.
I go to work on foot.
The subway is faster than the bus.
I need to buy a ticket.
How do you get to school?

grammar.explanation_en: Use 'by + transportation' to say how you travel: 'by bus', 'by car' (but 'on foot' for walking). To compare two things, add '-er' to short adjectives and use 'than': 'The subway is faster than the bus.'
grammar.explanation_ko: 어떻게 이동하는지 말할 때는 'by + 교통수단'을 씁니다: 'by bus', 'by car' (걷는 것만 예외로 'on foot'). 두 가지를 비교할 때는 짧은 형용사에 '-er'을 붙이고 'than'을 씁니다: 'The subway is faster than the bus.'(지하철이 버스보다 빨라요)

examples.en: I go to school by subway.
A taxi is more expensive than a bus.
Walking is slower than riding a bike.

reading.title: Getting to School
reading.text: Every morning, I go to school by bus. The bus is slower than the subway, but it is cheaper. My friend rides her bicycle to school. It only takes her ten minutes. On sunny days, I sometimes walk on foot.
reading.text_ko: 매일 아침 저는 버스로 학교에 가요. 버스는 지하철보다 느리지만 더 저렴해요. 제 친구는 자전거로 학교에 가요. 십 분밖에 안 걸려요. 화창한 날에는 가끔 걸어서 가요.

questions.prompt: 글쓴이는 매일 아침 어떻게 학교에 가나요?
